accepted_step.derivation: Alphabet order starts with A at index 1, so continuing consecutively gives A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4, E=5, F=6, G=7, H=8. For a first job J, initial setup is idx(J) mod 3. Reducing each index modulo 3 yields A:1 mod3=1, B:2 mod3=2, C:3 mod3=0, D:4 mod3=1, E:5 mod3=2, F:6 mod3=0, G:7 mod3=1, H:8 mod3=2. Between distinct consecutive jobs I,J, setup is abs(idx(I)-idx(J)) mod 3. This depends only on the two indices and is symmetric. Examples: s(A,B)=|1-2| mod3=1; s(A,C)=|1-3| mod3=2; s(C,D)=|3-4| mod3=1. Independently checking, all indices are assigned by consecutive alphabet position from A, and each modulo-3 reduction matches the stated 0/1/2 pattern. This step makes no scheduling choice; it fixes only setup inputs. No tested objections were supplied, so there are no objection dispositions to redo.

use.method: Check using alphabet index = ordinal position starting at A=1, then reduce modulo 3. Concrete public computation: A=1 -> 1 mod 3=1; B=2 -> 2 mod 3=2; C=3 -> 0; D=4 -> 1; E=5 -> 2; F=6 -> 0; G=7 -> 1; H=8 -> 2. Transition setup is abs(index difference) mod 3, e.g. s(A,B)=abs(1-2) mod 3=1, s(A,C)=abs(1-3) mod 3=2, s(C,D)=abs(3-4) mod 3=1. This reproduces the returned index assignment, initial setup values, transition formula, and examples.
